title: Understanding is the new bottleneck
excerpt: Agents can write code faster than we can absorb it. Here's why it still matters for humans to understand what they build — and some techniques for doing that efficiently: explainer docs, quizzes, micro-worlds, and shared spaces.
content_html:
Hot take: I think it's still important to understand the code that our agents write!

In this talk I'll explain why that's the case, and show some ideas for how to efficiently understand code. Alright, let's dive in.

Agents are writing more and more code for us, and we all know it's getting harder to keep up.

But the good news is: there are many ways to understand code! Reading diffs line by line is not the only way.

Most of this talk will be about techniques I have found helpful to understand systems my agents are building:

  • Code explainer docs
  • Quizzes to check my understanding
  • Micro-worlds that I can play with to understand the system

But first we have to ask a more basic question…

Why understand?

Why? Why understand?

Aren't we supposed to be taking ourselves out of the loop now, and letting the agents loop themselves? As the agents get smarter, doesn't it become less important for us to be in the details?

I think many people — even those who are pro-understanding — have a slightly incorrect answer to this question!

One possible answer: we understand to verify. We check the agent's work, we see if it's correct.

Correct can mean many things: does it match the spec, is it well architected… but it's fundamentally a thumbs-up / thumbs-down question.

Here's the thing: the agents are getting better and better at verifying their own work. And this is good! I like it when my agent doesn't make mistakes.

But hmm. Where does that leave us humans?

That's where another answer comes in: we can understand to participate.

You can learn what the agent is doing to make sure you can be an active participant in the creative process. Here's why this matters…

It's never just one loop! A project is many, many loops with the agent.

And the understanding you have of the system is part of your ability to come up with the next idea to evolve it.

You need a rich set of concepts in your mind to think creatively and fluently about how to move something forward. If you're lacking that fluency, your ability to participate in the project is meaningfully limited.

By the way, this relates closely to the idea of cognitive debt, popularized by Margaret Storey and Simon Willison.

It's like tech debt: you can get away with not understanding what's going on in the short term, but it'll bite you eventually.

OK, so fine, understanding matters.

But this raises the next question: how? How do we build this human understanding when we're working with AI and moving fast?

Well, turns out this is not the first time anyone has ever thought about how to communicate understanding. I think we can look to education as an inspiration. Can we steal the best ideas ever invented for education and apply them to this problem?

Technique 1: Explanations

Today I want to share three techniques that show how we can attempt this.

First: explanations. What makes a good explanation?

Whenever an agent finishes some work, it's an opportunity for an explanation — an artifact.

Most naively, we can read a code diff: the raw material that changed.

But what if we ask:

What would the best explanation be? If you had a team — human or AI — that really sweat the details of explaining something well to you, how would that feel?

Here's one answer. I made a skill called /explain-diff, which I use every day and many coworkers have found valuable.

It outputs thoughtfully structured code explainers as HTML, markdown, or Notion docs. Notion is a good place for collaborating on and discussing these explainers as a team. (Disclaimer: I work at Notion so I'm biased.)

Let's see what's in one of these explainers, using an example of editing the perspective of a video game.

First principle: teach me background info!

Before we even get to what changed, help me understand what was already there. In this case, teach me about the game engine.

Second principle: intuition before details.

Before any code, it states the goal — “make the garden feel three-dimensional with 2D drawing tricks” — and explains related concepts, like what isometric projection is.

All of this builds my intuition for the essence of the change. It's catching me up as the human so I can be an equal participant in understanding.

You can also build intuition with interactive figures.

Here I'm understanding the isometric perspective by dragging rocks around the garden and watching their coordinates move.

(This is using a new feature Notion just shipped: you can now embed interactive HTML inside pages.)

We finally get to the code. But a typical diff is a pile of files edited in alphabetical order with no explanation.

A “literate diff” as I call it is structured as prose — walking through the changes in a sensible order, with surrounding explanation and embedded code snippets. Faster to review than a raw diff.

The end result of all of this is a nice explainer packet. I still read the code diff but I always read this first.

Sometimes I'll print these out and take them to the café — less distracting.

It's beautifully ironic: AI turns an interactive activity into a static paper report I can focus on deeply :)

I do something similar with my code explainers now. At the bottom of an explainer there's an interactive quiz — five questions about the change — and I try to answer them.

My rule: I won't send code to others until I can pass the quiz, and I do the same when reviewing others' code.

A quiz is a speed regulator. Working with AI, it's easy for the loop to run faster than the speed of human understanding.

The quiz is a counterbalancing force: I mechanically ask “do I actually understand?” so that I can remain a full creative participant.

Technique 2: Micro-worlds

Next idea: micro-worlds. This one's inspired by the visionary educator Seymour Papert.

Papert had this beautiful idea he called living in Mathland: if you want to learn math, live in Mathland — just like if you want to learn French, you go live in France. Could we build an environment where children learn math naturally, as a consequence of their curiosity?

So how do we apply that to code? Can we make worlds you inhabit and naturally intuit how the system works and how it's changing?

Last year I was coding a Prolog interpreter and struggling to intuit what was happening inside.

I worked with an agent to build this debugger, which let me step through the execution of my logic language — scrub through time, see what's on the stack and which rules are evaluated at each step. I could even leave comments for myself (“nice, we correctly applied that rule”).

There's a big difference between making a tool for me to debug and letting the agent debug — doing it myself is how I develop understanding along the way.

Another example. I was migrating my personal website from one framework to another, and Claude wrote a script that did it. But it was very hard to review: I wasn't familiar with the new framework, and all I could say was “I guess that looks about right.”

So I asked Claude to make me a video game — a command center where I do the port myself, step by step, watching the visible effects and the file tree evolve. It produced a UI where I click buttons to run the port step by step, with my old site and new site running side by side.

In this command center I watched the new site come to life incrementally. That left me with a similar understanding to doing it by hand — but much faster, because the whole experience was laid out for me.

The point here is that agents can write bits of code that help us humans understand other code.

This is a big deal!

Technique 3: Shared spaces

Alright, last technique: shared spaces. So far this has all been about understanding solo… but when you're working on a team, you need to understand together.

When you and someone else hold the same mental model, you can communicate efficiently. You have a shared vocabulary that evokes the same images, so you can jam and riff and have creative conversations. Without those shared structures, those conversations are much harder.

I'm really excited about creating shared environments where teams build that understanding together. It's kinda what Notion is all about too.

Recently in Notion we've been shipping tons of new features for humans and agents to work together, so your whole team develops a shared understanding instead of each working in a silo.

One tiny example: you can now run Claude and Cursor agents in Notion. I do a lot of my coding that way now.

And when those agents make a technical plan in Notion, it's in a collaborative page by default, so I can comment on it with my team and discuss immediately. Thinking together, not alone!

The point was always to augment

Alright, let's wrap up. Today we've covered some techniques that were about understanding code… but actually I think this is a much bigger issue.

It's still important for humans to understand how things work in general! Not just to verify, but to participate.

And surprise surprise, this is not a new idea. It harkens back to the very origins of our field of computing…

50 years ago Alan Kay envisioned that computers could be a new medium, better than the book, for teaching people — especially kids — how to think about the world.

In this picture, it might look like these kids are watching YouTube on an iPad, but they're not. They're playing an interactive game and editing the code as they play it to get a better understanding of physics. This was 50 years ago!!

And now hopefully you understand this meme.

The point was always to augment, not just automate.

It's beautiful that AI now makes creating simulations so accessible… Having AI teach us is one of the greatest possibilities computing has ever opened up.

This makes me very optimistic about the future!

If we build the right tools, we can now understand the world better than we ever could before. We don't have to merely take ourselves out of the loop, we can get deeper in the loop too. It's up to us.

FIN

Related reads

If you enjoyed this talk, you might like these other posts I've written about human-AI collaboration:

  • Enough AI copilots! We need AI HUDs — "anyone serious about designing for AI should consider non-copilot form factors that more directly extend the human mind..."
  • AI-generated tools can make programming more fun — "Instead, I used AI to build a custom debugger UI… which made it more fun for me to do the coding myself..."
  • Code like a surgeon — "identify and delegate the secondary grunt work tasks, so you can focus on the main thing that matters."

blocks.html_en: Whenever an agent finishes some work, it's an opportunity for an explanation — an artifact.

sentences.en: Whenever an agent finishes some work, it's an opportunity for an explanation — an artifact.
sentences.zh: 每当代理完成一些工作时，这就是一个解释的机会——一个工件。

blocks.html_en: Most naively, we can read a code diff: the raw material that changed.

sentences.en: Most naively, we can read a code diff: the raw material that changed.
sentences.zh: 最天真地，我们可以读取代码差异：更改的原材料。

blocks.html_en: But what if we ask:

sentences.en: But what if we ask:
sentences.zh: 但如果我们问：

blocks.html_en: What would the best explanation be? If you had a team — human or AI — that really sweat the details of explaining something well to you, how would that feel?

sentences.en: What would the best explanation be?
sentences.zh: 最好的解释是什么？

sentences.en: If you had a team — human or AI — that really sweat the details of explaining something well to you, how would that feel?
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个团队（无论是人类还是人工智能），他们非常注重向你解释某些细节的细节，那感觉如何？

blocks.html_en: Here's one answer. I made a skill called /explain-diff, which I use every day and many coworkers have found valuable.

sentences.en: Here's one answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个答案。

sentences.en: I made a skill called /explain-diff, which I use every day and many coworkers have found valuable.
sentences.zh: 我开发了一项名为 /explain-diff 的技能，我每天都在使用它，许多同事都发现它很有价值。

blocks.html_en: It outputs thoughtfully structured code explainers as HTML, markdown, or Notion docs. Notion is a good place for collaborating on and discussing these explainers as a team. (Disclaimer: I work at Notion so I'm biased.)

sentences.en: It outputs thoughtfully structured code explainers as HTML, markdown, or Notion docs.
sentences.zh: 它将精心构造的代码解释器输出为 HTML、markdown 或 Notion 文档。

sentences.en: Notion is a good place for collaborating on and discussing these explainers as a team.
sentences.zh: Notion 是团队协作和讨论这些解释器的好地方。

sentences.en: (Disclaimer: I work at Notion so I'm biased.)
sentences.zh: （免责声明：我在 Notion 工作，所以我有偏见。）

blocks.html_en: Let's see what's in one of these explainers, using an example of editing the perspective of a video game.

sentences.en: Let's see what's in one of these explainers, using an example of editing the perspective of a video game.
sentences.zh: 让我们以编辑视频游戏视角的示例来看看这些解释器中的内容。

blocks.html_en: First principle: teach me background info!

sentences.en: First principle: teach me background info!
sentences.zh: 第一个原则：教我背景信息！

blocks.html_en: Before we even get to what changed, help me understand what was already there. In this case, teach me about the game engine.

sentences.en: Before we even get to what changed, help me understand what was already there.
sentences.zh: 在我们了解发生了什么变化之前，请帮助我了解已经存在的内容。

sentences.en: In this case, teach me about the game engine.
sentences.zh: 既然如此，请教我有关游戏引擎的知识。

blocks.html_en: Second principle: intuition before details.

sentences.en: Second principle: intuition before details.
sentences.zh: 第二个原则：直觉优先于细节。

blocks.html_en: Before any code, it states the goal — “make the garden feel three-dimensional with 2D drawing tricks” — and explains related concepts, like what isometric projection is.

sentences.en: Before any code, it states the goal — “make the garden feel three-dimensional with 2D drawing tricks” — and explains related concepts, like what isometric projection is.
sentences.zh: 在任何代码之前，它都会陈述目标——“通过 2D 绘图技巧让花园感觉是三维的”——并解释相关概念，比如什么是等角投影。

blocks.html_en: All of this builds my intuition for the essence of the change. It's catching me up as the human so I can be an equal participant in understanding.

sentences.en: All of this builds my intuition for the essence of the change.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都构建了我对变革本质的直觉。

sentences.en: It's catching me up as the human so I can be an equal participant in understanding.
sentences.zh: 它让我成为人类，这样我就可以成为理解的平等参与者。

blocks.html_en: You can also build intuition with interactive figures.

sentences.en: You can also build intuition with interactive figures.
sentences.zh: 您还可以通过交互式图形建立直觉。

blocks.html_en: Here I'm understanding the isometric perspective by dragging rocks around the garden and watching their coordinates move.

sentences.en: Here I'm understanding the isometric perspective by dragging rocks around the garden and watching their coordinates move.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我通过在花园周围拖动岩石并观察它们的坐标移动来理解等距透视。

blocks.html_en: (This is using a new feature Notion just shipped: you can now embed interactive HTML inside pages.)

sentences.en: (This is using a new feature Notion just shipped: you can now embed interactive HTML inside pages.)
sentences.zh: （这是使用刚刚发布的一项新功能 Notion：您现在可以在页面内嵌入交互式 HTML。）

blocks.html_en: We finally get to the code. But a typical diff is a pile of files edited in alphabetical order with no explanation.

sentences.en: We finally get to the code.
sentences.zh: 我们终于看到代码了。

sentences.en: But a typical diff is a pile of files edited in alphabetical order with no explanation.
sentences.zh: 但典型的差异是一堆按字母顺序编辑的文件，没有任何解释。

blocks.html_en: A “literate diff” as I call it is structured as prose — walking through the changes in a sensible order, with surrounding explanation and embedded code snippets. Faster to review than a raw diff.

sentences.en: A “literate diff” as I call it is structured as prose — walking through the changes in a sensible order, with surrounding explanation and embedded code snippets.
sentences.zh: 我称之为“文学差异”，它的结构就像散文一样——以合理的顺序遍历更改，并附有周围的解释和嵌入的代码片段。

sentences.en: Faster to review than a raw diff.
sentences.zh: 比原始差异的审查速度更快。

blocks.html_en: The end result of all of this is a nice explainer packet. I still read the code diff but I always read this first.

sentences.en: The end result of all of this is a nice explainer packet.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切的最终结果是一个很好的解释包。

sentences.en: I still read the code diff but I always read this first.
sentences.zh: 我仍然阅读代码差异，但我总是先阅读这个。

blocks.html_en: Sometimes I'll print these out and take them to the café — less distracting.

sentences.en: Sometimes I'll print these out and take them to the café — less distracting.
sentences.zh: 有时我会把这些打印出来并带到咖啡馆——这样不会分散注意力。

blocks.html_en: It's beautifully ironic: AI turns an interactive activity into a static paper report I can focus on deeply :)

sentences.en: It's beautifully ironic: AI turns an interactive activity into a static paper report I can focus on deeply :)
sentences.zh: 这是非常讽刺的：人工智能将交互式活动变成了我可以深入关注的静态纸质报告:)

blocks.html_en: I do something similar with my code explainers now. At the bottom of an explainer there's an interactive quiz — five questions about the change — and I try to answer them.

sentences.en: I do something similar with my code explainers now.
sentences.zh: 我现在用我的代码解释器做类似的事情。

sentences.en: At the bottom of an explainer there's an interactive quiz — five questions about the change — and I try to answer them.
sentences.zh: 在解释器的底部有一个互动测验 - 五个有关更改的问题 - 我尝试回答它们。

blocks.html_en: My rule: I won't send code to others until I can pass the quiz, and I do the same when reviewing others' code.

sentences.en: My rule: I won't send code to others until I can pass the quiz, and I do the same when reviewing others' code.
sentences.zh: 我的规则：在通过测验之前我不会向其他人发送代码，并且在审查其他人的代码时我也会这样做。

blocks.html_en: A quiz is a speed regulator. Working with AI, it's easy for the loop to run faster than the speed of human understanding.

sentences.en: A quiz is a speed regulator.
sentences.zh: 测验是速度调节器。

sentences.en: Working with AI, it's easy for the loop to run faster than the speed of human understanding.
sentences.zh: 与人工智能一起工作，循环的运行速度很容易超过人类理解的速度。

blocks.html_en: The quiz is a counterbalancing force: I mechanically ask “do I actually understand?” so that I can remain a full creative participant.

sentences.en: The quiz is a counterbalancing force: I mechanically ask “do I actually understand?”
sentences.zh: 测验是一种平衡力量：我机械地问“我真的理解了吗？”

sentences.en: so that I can remain a full creative participant.
sentences.zh: 这样我就可以继续成为一名富有创造力的参与者。

blocks.html_en: Technique 2: Micro-worlds

sentences.en: Technique 2: Micro-worlds
sentences.zh: 技术 2：微观世界

blocks.html_en: Next idea: micro-worlds. This one's inspired by the visionary educator Seymour Papert.

sentences.en: Next idea: micro-worlds.
sentences.zh: 下一个想法：微观世界。

sentences.en: This one's inspired by the visionary educator Seymour Papert.
sentences.zh: 这是受到有远见的教育家 Seymour Papert 的启发。

blocks.html_en: Papert had this beautiful idea he called living in Mathland: if you want to learn math, live in Mathland — just like if you want to learn French, you go live in France. Could we build an environment where children learn math naturally, as a consequence of their curiosity?

sentences.en: Papert had this beautiful idea he called living in Mathland: if you want to learn math, live in Mathland — just like if you want to learn French, you go live in France.
sentences.zh: 帕普特有一个美好的想法，他称之为“住在Mathland”：如果你想学习数学，就住在Mathland——就像如果你想学习法语，就住在法国一样。

sentences.en: Could we build an environment where children learn math naturally, as a consequence of their curiosity?
sentences.zh: 我们能否营造一个让孩子们出于好奇心而自然地学习数学的环境？

blocks.html_en: So how do we apply that to code? Can we make worlds you inhabit and naturally intuit how the system works and how it's changing?

sentences.en: So how do we apply that to code?
sentences.zh: 那么我们如何将其应用到代码中呢？

sentences.en: Can we make worlds you inhabit and naturally intuit how the system works and how it's changing?
sentences.zh: 我们能否创造一个让你居住的世界，并自然地凭直觉了解系统如何运作以及如何变化？

blocks.html_en: Last year I was coding a Prolog interpreter and struggling to intuit what was happening inside.

sentences.en: Last year I was coding a Prolog interpreter and struggling to intuit what was happening inside.
sentences.zh: 去年，我正在编写一个 Prolog 解释器，并努力凭直觉了解内部发生的情况。

blocks.html_en: I worked with an agent to build this debugger, which let me step through the execution of my logic language — scrub through time, see what's on the stack and which rules are evaluated at each step. I could even leave comments for myself (“nice, we correctly applied that rule”).

sentences.en: I worked with an agent to build this debugger, which let me step through the execution of my logic language — scrub through time, see what's on the stack and which rules are evaluated at each step.
sentences.zh: 我与一个代理一起构建了这个调试器，它让我可以逐步执行逻辑语言 - 浏览时间，查看堆栈上有什么以及每一步评估哪些规则。

sentences.en: I could even leave comments for myself (“nice, we correctly applied that rule”).
sentences.zh: 我什至可以为自己留下评论（“很好，我们正确地应用了该规则”）。

blocks.html_en: There's a big difference between making a tool for me to debug and letting the agent debug — doing it myself is how I develop understanding along the way.

sentences.en: There's a big difference between making a tool for me to debug and letting the agent debug — doing it myself is how I develop understanding along the way.
sentences.zh: 制作一个工具供我调试和让代理调试之间有很大的区别——我自己动手调试是我一路上发展理解的方式。

blocks.html_en: Another example. I was migrating my personal website from one framework to another, and Claude wrote a script that did it. But it was very hard to review: I wasn't familiar with the new framework, and all I could say was “I guess that looks about right.”

sentences.en: Another example.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子。

sentences.en: I was migrating my personal website from one framework to another, and Claude wrote a script that did it.
sentences.zh: 我正在将我的个人网站从一个框架迁移到另一个框架，克劳德编写了一个脚本来完成这件事。

sentences.en: But it was very hard to review: I wasn't familiar with the new framework, and all I could say was “I guess that looks about right.”
sentences.zh: 但审查起来非常困难：我不熟悉新框架，我只能说“我想这看起来不错”。

blocks.html_en: So I asked Claude to make me a video game — a command center where I do the port myself, step by step, watching the visible effects and the file tree evolve. It produced a UI where I click buttons to run the port step by step, with my old site and new site running side by side.

sentences.en: So I asked Claude to make me a video game — a command center where I do the port myself, step by step, watching the visible effects and the file tree evolve.
sentences.zh: 因此，我要求克劳德为我制作一个视频游戏——一个指挥中心，我自己在其中一步步进行移植，观察可见的效果和文件树的演变。

sentences.en: It produced a UI where I click buttons to run the port step by step, with my old site and new site running side by side.
sentences.zh: 它生成了一个用户界面，我可以在其中单击按钮逐步运行端口，旧站点和新站点并排运行。

blocks.html_en: In this command center I watched the new site come to life incrementally. That left me with a similar understanding to doing it by hand — but much faster, because the whole experience was laid out for me.

sentences.en: In this command center I watched the new site come to life incrementally.
sentences.zh: 在这个指挥中心，我目睹了新站点的逐步上线。

sentences.en: That left me with a similar understanding to doing it by hand — but much faster, because the whole experience was laid out for me.
sentences.zh: 这让我对手工操作有了类似的理解，但速度更快，因为整个体验都是为我准备的。

blocks.html_en: The point here is that agents can write bits of code that help us humans understand other code.

sentences.en: The point here is that agents can write bits of code that help us humans understand other code.
sentences.zh: 这里的要点是，代理可以编写一些代码来帮助我们人类理解其他代码。

blocks.html_en: This is a big deal!

sentences.en: This is a big deal!
sentences.zh: 这是一件大事！

blocks.html_en: Technique 3: Shared spaces

sentences.en: Technique 3: Shared spaces
sentences.zh: 技巧 3：共享空间

blocks.html_en: Alright, last technique: shared spaces. So far this has all been about understanding solo… but when you're working on a team, you need to understand together.

sentences.en: Alright, last technique: shared spaces.
sentences.zh: 好吧，最后一个技巧：共享空间。

sentences.en: So far this has all been about understanding solo…
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，这都是关于单独理解......

sentences.en: but when you're working on a team, you need to understand together.
sentences.zh: 但当你在一个团队中工作时，你需要一起理解。

blocks.html_en: When you and someone else hold the same mental model, you can communicate efficiently. You have a shared vocabulary that evokes the same images, so you can jam and riff and have creative conversations. Without those shared structures, those conversations are much harder.

sentences.en: When you and someone else hold the same mental model, you can communicate efficiently.
sentences.zh: 当你和别人持有相同的心理模型时，你们就能有效地沟通。

sentences.en: You have a shared vocabulary that evokes the same images, so you can jam and riff and have creative conversations.
sentences.zh: 你们拥有共同的词汇，可以唤起相同的图像，因此你们可以即兴演奏、即兴发挥并进行富有创意的对话。

sentences.en: Without those shared structures, those conversations are much harder.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这些共享的结构，这些对话就会困难得多。

blocks.html_en: I'm really excited about creating shared environments where teams build that understanding together. It's kinda what Notion is all about too.

sentences.en: I'm really excited about creating shared environments where teams build that understanding together.
sentences.zh: 我对创建共享环境感到非常兴奋，团队可以在其中共同建立这种理解。

sentences.en: It's kinda what Notion is all about too.
sentences.zh: 这也是 Notion 的全部内容。

blocks.html_en: Recently in Notion we've been shipping tons of new features for humans and agents to work together, so your whole team develops a shared understanding instead of each working in a silo.

sentences.en: Recently in Notion we've been shipping tons of new features for humans and agents to work together, so your whole team develops a shared understanding instead of each working in a silo.
sentences.zh: 最近，我们在 Notion 中发布了大量新功能，供人类和智能体协同工作，因此您的整个团队可以形成共同的理解，而不是各自为政。

blocks.html_en: One tiny example: you can now run Claude and Cursor agents in Notion. I do a lot of my coding that way now.

sentences.en: One tiny example: you can now run Claude and Cursor agents in Notion.
sentences.zh: 举一个小例子：您现在可以在 Notion 中运行 Claude 和 Cursor 代理。

sentences.en: I do a lot of my coding that way now.
sentences.zh: 我现在用这种方式做很多编码。

blocks.html_en: And when those agents make a technical plan in Notion, it's in a collaborative page by default, so I can comment on it with my team and discuss immediately. Thinking together, not alone!

sentences.en: And when those agents make a technical plan in Notion, it's in a collaborative page by default, so I can comment on it with my team and discuss immediately.
sentences.zh: 当这些代理在 Notion 中制定技术计划时，它默认位于协作页面中，因此我可以与我的团队对其进行评论并立即进行讨论。

sentences.en: Thinking together, not alone!
sentences.zh: 一起思考，而不是单独思考！

blocks.html_en: The point was always to augment

sentences.en: The point was always to augment
sentences.zh: 重点始终是增强

blocks.html_en: Alright, let's wrap up. Today we've covered some techniques that were about understanding code… but actually I think this is a much bigger issue.

sentences.en: Alright, let's wrap up.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们结束吧。

sentences.en: Today we've covered some techniques that were about understanding code…
sentences.zh: 今天我们介绍了一些关于理解代码的技术……

sentences.en: but actually I think this is a much bigger issue.
sentences.zh: 但实际上我认为这是一个更大的问题。

blocks.html_en: It's still important for humans to understand how things work in general! Not just to verify, but to participate.

sentences.en: It's still important for humans to understand how things work in general!
sentences.zh: 对于人类来说，了解事物的总体运作方式仍然很重要！

sentences.en: Not just to verify, but to participate.
sentences.zh: 不仅要验证，还要参与。

blocks.html_en: And surprise surprise, this is not a new idea. It harkens back to the very origins of our field of computing…

sentences.en: And surprise surprise, this is not a new idea.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，这并不是一个新想法。

sentences.en: It harkens back to the very origins of our field of computing…
sentences.zh: 它可以追溯到我们计算领域的起源……

blocks.html_en: 50 years ago Alan Kay envisioned that computers could be a new medium, better than the book, for teaching people — especially kids — how to think about the world.

sentences.en: 50 years ago Alan Kay envisioned that computers could be a new medium, better than the book, for teaching people — especially kids — how to think about the world.
sentences.zh: 50 年前，艾伦·凯 (Alan Kay) 设想计算机可能成为一种比书本更好的新媒介，可以教人们（尤其是孩子）如何思考世界。

blocks.html_en: In this picture, it might look like these kids are watching YouTube on an iPad, but they're not. They're playing an interactive game and editing the code as they play it to get a better understanding of physics. This was 50 years ago!!

sentences.en: In this picture, it might look like these kids are watching YouTube on an iPad, but they're not.
sentences.zh: 在这张照片中，这些孩子可能看起来像是在 iPad 上观看 YouTube，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: They're playing an interactive game and editing the code as they play it to get a better understanding of physics.
sentences.zh: 他们正在玩一个交互式游戏，并在玩游戏时编辑代码，以更好地理解物理。

sentences.en: This was 50 years ago!!
sentences.zh: 这是50年前的事了！！

blocks.html_en: And now hopefully you understand this meme.

sentences.en: And now hopefully you understand this meme.
sentences.zh: 现在希望你能理解这个模因。

blocks.html_en: The point was always to augment, not just automate.

sentences.en: The point was always to augment, not just automate.
sentences.zh: 重点始终是增强，而不仅仅是自动化。

blocks.html_en: It's beautiful that AI now makes creating simulations so accessible… Having AI teach us is one of the greatest possibilities computing has ever opened up.

sentences.en: It's beautiful that AI now makes creating simulations so accessible…
sentences.zh: 人工智能现在让创建模拟变得如此容易，这真是太棒了……

sentences.en: Having AI teach us is one of the greatest possibilities computing has ever opened up.
sentences.zh: 让人工智能来教我们是计算技术带来的最大可能性之一。

blocks.html_en: This makes me very optimistic about the future!

sentences.en: This makes me very optimistic about the future!
sentences.zh: 这让我对未来非常乐观！

blocks.html_en: If we build the right tools, we can now understand the world better than we ever could before. We don't have to merely take ourselves out of the loop, we can get deeper in the loop too. It's up to us.

sentences.en: If we build the right tools, we can now understand the world better than we ever could before.
sentences.zh: 如果我们构建正确的工具，我们现在可以比以前更好地了解世界。

sentences.en: We don't have to merely take ourselves out of the loop, we can get deeper in the loop too.
sentences.zh: 我们不必仅仅让自己脱离循环，我们也可以更深入地陷入循环。

sentences.en: It's up to us.
sentences.zh: 这取决于我们。

blocks.html_en: FIN
Related reads

sentences.en: Related reads
sentences.zh: 相关阅读

blocks.html_en: If you enjoyed this talk, you might like these other posts I've written about human-AI collaboration:

sentences.en: If you enjoyed this talk, you might like these other posts I've written about human-AI collaboration:
sentences.zh: 如果您喜欢这次演讲，您可能会喜欢我写的有关人类与人工智能协作的其他帖子：

blocks.html_en: • Enough AI copilots! We need AI HUDs — "anyone serious about designing for AI should consider non-copilot form factors that more directly extend the human mind..."

sentences.en: Enough AI copilots!
sentences.zh: 人工智能副驾驶已经够多了！

sentences.en: We need AI HUDs — "anyone serious about designing for AI should consider non-copilot form factors that more directly extend the human mind..."
sentences.zh: 我们需要人工智能 HUD——“任何认真考虑人工智能设计的人都应该考虑非副驾驶的外形因素，更直接地扩展人类思维……”

blocks.html_en: • AI-generated tools can make programming more fun — "Instead, I used AI to build a custom debugger UI… which made it more fun for me to do the coding myself..."

sentences.en: AI-generated tools can make programming more fun — "Instead, I used AI to build a custom debugger UI…
sentences.zh: AI 生成的工具可以让编程变得更加有趣——“相反，我使用 AI 构建了自定义调试器 UI......

sentences.en: which made it more fun for me to do the coding myself..."

content_html_zh:
热门观点：我认为理解我们的代理编写的代码仍然很重要！

在本次演讲中，我将解释为什么会出现这种情况，并展示一些如何有效理解代码的想法。 好吧，让我们深入了解一下。

代理正在为我们编写越来越多的代码，我们都知道跟上步伐变得越来越困难。

但好消息是：理解代码的方法有很多！ 逐行读取差异并不是唯一的方法。

本次演讲的大部分内容将讨论我发现有助于理解我的代理正在构建的系统的技术：

  • 代码解释器文档
  • 通过测验来检查我的理解情况
  • 我可以通过玩弄微观世界来理解系统

但首先我们必须问一个更基本的问题......

为什么懂？

为什么？ 为什么懂？

难道我们现在不应该让自己脱离循环，让特工自己循环吗？ 随着代理变得越来越聪明，我们关注细节不是变得不那么重要了吗？

我想很多人——甚至那些支持理解的人——对这个问题的答案都有点不正确！

一种可能的答案是：我们了解核实。 我们检查代理的工作，看看它是否正确。

正确可能意味着很多事情：它是否符合规范，它的架构是否良好...... 但这从根本上来说是一个赞成/反对的问题。

事情是这样的：代理人在验证自己的工作方面做得越来越好。 这很好！ 我喜欢我的经纪人不犯错误。

但是嗯。 这让我们人类何去何从？

这就是另一个答案的来源：我们可以理解参与。

您可以了解代理正在做什么，以确保您可以积极参与创作过程。 这就是为什么这很重要......

它绝不只是一个循环！ 一个项目有很多很多与代理的循环。

你对系统的理解是你提出下一个想法来改进它的能力的一部分。

你的头脑中需要有一套丰富的概念，才能创造性地、流畅地思考如何推动事情向前发展。 如果您缺乏这种流畅性，那么您参与该项目的能力就会受到极大的限制。

顺便说一句，这与玛格丽特·斯托里和西蒙·威利森推广的认知债务概念密切相关。

这就像技术债务：你可以在短期内不了解正在发生的事情，但它最终会咬你一口。

好吧，很好，理解很重要。

但这提出了下一个问题：如何？ 当我们使用人工智能并快速发展时，我们如何建立这种人类理解？

事实证明，这并不是有人第一次思考如何沟通理解。 我认为我们可以将教育视为一种灵感。 我们能否窃取有史以来最好的教育理念并将其应用于这个问题？

技巧 1：解释

今天我想分享三种技术来展示我们如何尝试这一点。

第一：解释。 什么才是好的解释？

每当代理完成一些工作时，这就是一个解释的机会——一个工件。

最天真地，我们可以读取代码差异：更改的原材料。

但如果我们问：

最好的解释是什么？ 如果你有一个团队（无论是人类还是人工智能），他们非常注重向你解释某些细节的细节，那感觉如何？

这是一个答案。 我开发了一项名为 /explain-diff 的技能，我每天都在使用它，许多同事都发现它很有价值。

它将精心构造的代码解释器输出为 HTML、markdown 或 Notion 文档。 Notion 是团队协作和讨论这些解释器的好地方。 （免责声明：我在 Notion 工作，所以我有偏见。）

让我们以编辑视频游戏视角的示例来看看这些解释器中的内容。

第一个原则：教我背景信息！

在我们了解发生了什么变化之前，请帮助我了解已经存在的内容。 既然如此，请教我有关游戏引擎的知识。

第二个原则：直觉优先于细节。

在任何代码之前，它都会陈述目标——“通过 2D 绘图技巧让花园感觉是三维的”——并解释相关概念，比如什么是等角投影。

所有这些都构建了我对变革本质的直觉。 它让我成为人类，这样我就可以成为理解的平等参与者。

您还可以通过交互式图形建立直觉。

在这里，我通过在花园周围拖动岩石并观察它们的坐标移动来理解等距透视。

（这是使用刚刚发布的一项新功能 Notion：您现在可以在页面内嵌入交互式 HTML。）

我们终于看到代码了。 但典型的差异是一堆按字母顺序编辑的文件，没有任何解释。

我称之为“文学差异”，它的结构就像散文一样——以合理的顺序遍历更改，并附有周围的解释和嵌入的代码片段。 比原始差异的审查速度更快。

所有这一切的最终结果是一个很好的解释包。 我仍然阅读代码差异，但我总是先阅读这个。

有时我会把这些打印出来并带到咖啡馆——这样不会分散注意力。

这是非常讽刺的：人工智能将交互式活动变成了我可以深入关注的静态纸质报告:)

我现在用我的代码解释器做类似的事情。 在解释器的底部有一个互动测验 - 五个有关更改的问题 - 我尝试回答它们。

我的规则：在通过测验之前我不会向其他人发送代码，并且在审查其他人的代码时我也会这样做。

测验是速度调节器。 与人工智能一起工作，循环的运行速度很容易超过人类理解的速度。

测验是一种平衡力量：我机械地问“我真的理解了吗？” 这样我就可以继续成为一名富有创造力的参与者。

技术 2：微观世界

下一个想法：微观世界。 这是受到有远见的教育家 Seymour Papert 的启发。

帕普特有一个美好的想法，他称之为“住在Mathland”：如果你想学习数学，就住在Mathland——就像如果你想学习法语，就住在法国一样。 我们能否营造一个让孩子们出于好奇心而自然地学习数学的环境？

那么我们如何将其应用到代码中呢？ 我们能否创造一个让你居住的世界，并自然地凭直觉了解系统如何运作以及如何变化？

去年，我正在编写一个 Prolog 解释器，并努力凭直觉了解内部发生的情况。

我与一个代理一起构建了这个调试器，它让我可以逐步执行逻辑语言 - 浏览时间，查看堆栈上有什么以及每一步评估哪些规则。 我什至可以为自己留下评论（“很好，我们正确地应用了该规则”）。

制作一个工具供我调试和让代理调试之间有很大的区别——我自己动手调试是我一路上发展理解的方式。

另一个例子。 我正在将我的个人网站从一个框架迁移到另一个框架，克劳德编写了一个脚本来完成这件事。 但审查起来非常困难：我不熟悉新框架，我只能说“我想这看起来不错”。

因此，我要求克劳德为我制作一个视频游戏——一个指挥中心，我自己在其中一步步进行移植，观察可见的效果和文件树的演变。 它生成了一个用户界面，我可以在其中单击按钮逐步运行端口，旧站点和新站点并排运行。

在这个指挥中心，我目睹了新站点的逐步上线。 这让我对手工操作有了类似的理解，但速度更快，因为整个体验都是为我准备的。

这里的要点是，代理可以编写一些代码来帮助我们人类理解其他代码。

这是一件大事！

技巧 3：共享空间

好吧，最后一个技巧：共享空间。 到目前为止，这都是关于单独理解...... 但当你在一个团队中工作时，你需要一起理解。

当你和别人持有相同的心理模型时，你们就能有效地沟通。 你们拥有共同的词汇，可以唤起相同的图像，因此你们可以即兴演奏、即兴发挥并进行富有创意的对话。 如果没有这些共享的结构，这些对话就会困难得多。

我对创建共享环境感到非常兴奋，团队可以在其中共同建立这种理解。 这也是 Notion 的全部内容。

最近，我们在 Notion 中发布了大量新功能，供人类和智能体协同工作，因此您的整个团队可以形成共同的理解，而不是各自为政。

举一个小例子：您现在可以在 Notion 中运行 Claude 和 Cursor 代理。 我现在用这种方式做很多编码。

当这些代理在 Notion 中制定技术计划时，它默认位于协作页面中，因此我可以与我的团队对其进行评论并立即进行讨论。 一起思考，而不是单独思考！

重点始终是增强

好吧，让我们结束吧。 今天我们介绍了一些关于理解代码的技术…… 但实际上我认为这是一个更大的问题。

对于人类来说，了解事物的总体运作方式仍然很重要！ 不仅要验证，还要参与。

令人惊讶的是，这并不是一个新想法。 它可以追溯到我们计算领域的起源……

50 年前，艾伦·凯 (Alan Kay) 设想计算机可能成为一种比书本更好的新媒介，可以教人们（尤其是孩子）如何思考世界。

在这张照片中，这些孩子可能看起来像是在 iPad 上观看 YouTube，但事实并非如此。 他们正在玩一个交互式游戏，并在玩游戏时编辑代码，以更好地理解物理。 这是50年前的事了！！

现在希望你能理解这个模因。

重点始终是增强，而不仅仅是自动化。

人工智能现在让创建模拟变得如此容易，这真是太棒了…… 让人工智能来教我们是计算技术带来的最大可能性之一。

这让我对未来非常乐观！

如果我们构建正确的工具，我们现在可以比以前更好地了解世界。 我们不必仅仅让自己脱离循环，我们也可以更深入地陷入循环。 这取决于我们。

FIN
